title: Investigate burst config shadowing causing cross-tenant token leakage and 429s
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers experienced sudden 429s across Hosted and Dedicated fleets during a config roll (2026-03-09). Investigation shows a config shadowing bug plus a config-reload race allowed per-tenant burst buckets to be replaced with a shared in-memory token source on edge proxies, leading to cross-tenant token leakage and rapid depletion for active tenants. Impact: three customers reported degraded service (large batch requesters and streaming clients), automated fallbacks tripped, and SRE escalated to SEV2. Reproduction: 1) Start with a cluster running default global burst policy and a subset of tenants with custom per-tenant burst overrides. 2) Trigger a config push that adds/removes per-tenant overrides while edge proxies reload concurrently. 3) Observe that some proxies swap their token_bucket pointer to a global allocator due to an initialization ordering bug, causing one tenant's high throughput to consume tokens for others. Root cause (hypothesis validated by heap snapshots and logs): an allocator-instance was stored in the proxy's non-atomic map with a key collision during hot-reload; when per-tenant config was removed/added rapidly, the map returned a fallback allocator instance that was shared between entries. Additionally, serialization format mismatch between the control-plane writer and edge reader caused an incorrect "burst_window" defaulting to seconds vs milliseconds in one code path, amplifying the leakage window. Immediate mitigations: - Reverted the recent config propagation change (control-plane) to stop new rollouts. - Applied emergency per-tenant hard caps on the gateway for impacted customers to avoid cross-tenant bleed. - Rolled out a hotfix that makes token allocator references immutable during reload; scoped to a single proxy pool and monitored for regressions. Permanent fix plan: 1) Change config reload to use a copy-on-write map and atomic swaps for per-tenant allocators. 2) Add strict schema validation and end-to-end serialization tests for burst_window units. 3) Add unit & e2e tests simulating rapid add/remove tenant overrides and CI guard. 4) Backfill observability: per-proxy token allocator id in traces and a Grafana panel for allocator churn. Owner: Marco Rivera. Next steps: patch review, CI e2e run, canary to 5% traffic then 25% then full. Postmortem draft (link) once customer comms complete.
